appendix.title: Pitfalls
appendix.para: The bridge's rules are few, and each follows from a difference between Rexx and .NET. These are the places where they surprise.

varlistentry.term: A Rexx string prefers a string parameter

listitem.para: .net~System~Convert~ToBoolean(1) calls ToBoolean(string), which wants "True", and fails; sb~Append("007") appends 007. Force the type the call means: .net~int32(1) (). Indexers are the exception: a whole number is a position ().
A .NET array is a Rexx Array: bytes[1] is its first element. A List keeps .NET's indexing: list[0]. .NET's own members of an array (GetValue, IndexOf) count from 0, as .NET documents them.

varlistentry.term: say shows the proxy, not .NET's text

listitem.para: say sb shows a NetObject (System.Text.StringBuilder #12); say sb~ToString shows its text. An enum value and an array are the exceptions: they show their name and their elements.

varlistentry.term: Rexx's methods win, but for six names

listitem.para: class, isA, objectName, hashCode and the other methods of Rexx's Object and of NetObject are Rexx's: a .NET member with such a name is reached with .net~invoke(o, "Name"). start, send, copy, run, request and string go to .NET when it has them ().
form~Location~X = 5 changes a copy; set the whole value ().
A handler fits a delegate that returns nothing before one that returns a value, so Task.Run takes it as an Action. .net~as(h, "System.Func<int>") chooses the other ().

varlistentry.term: A handler that waits for its object's guard

listitem.para: A handler called from another thread waits while its object runs a guarded method; a window's object waiting in Application.Run, or a loop, keeps it waiting for ever. Make handler methods UNGUARDED ().

varlistentry.term: await on a user interface thread

listitem.para: Awaiting a task that needs the user interface's thread, on that thread, never ends ().

varlistentry.term: One Rexx method for every overload

listitem.para: A Rexx class that extends a .NET class overrides every overload of a name with one method: Write of a TextWriter gets a char, a string, a char[], a format and its arguments. Look at what arrives ().
An entry of .local named as a Rexx class (LIST, ARRAY, FILE) is hidden by the class: .list is Rexx's List. A .NET host should give its objects other names ().
rexx.Run(".directory~new") runs that expression as a command; a routine returns its value: rexx.Run("return .directory~new").
